en.title: Minimizer of a Convex Quadratic on an Interval
en.description:
Each query gives a convex quadratic function f(x)=Ax²+Bx+C and a closed interval [left,right]; find the x that minimizes the function value, not the minimum value itself. Round the result to six decimal places; when the true value lies exactly at the midpoint between two six-decimal numbers, either rounding is accepted.

This site's standard input/output is stated explicitly; ranges not given by the source are all marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains q, followed by q lines of A B C left right. This site's integer protocol: 1≤q≤1000, 1≤A≤10⁶, B/C/left/right are in −10⁶..10⁶, and left≤right.
en.output: For each query, output one line with the minimizer x, which must have six decimal places.
en.explanation: Example 1: the three unconstrained minimizers are 2, −1, and 2; after restricting to the corresponding intervals, the outputs are 2.000000, 0.000000, and 3.000000. Example 2: the minimizer is −0.0000005, so both −0.000001 and 0.000000 are valid. Example 3: the minimizer is 1/3, so the output is 0.333333.
hints: Use ternary search with high-precision Decimal, narrowing the interval that contains the minimizer using only function evaluations, and finally round to six decimal places.
